title.narrative: ROAF/Uganda/Emergency Technical Support For Rehabilitating The Kiteezi Dumpsite Through Implementation Of The Fukuoka Method.

description.narrative:
The Emergency Technical Support for Rehabilitating the Kiteezi Dumpsite is a transformative initiative designed to address the ongoing fires, contamination of the riverine system with leachate and recurrence of landslides and loss of lives and properties at the Kiteezi Dumpsitein Kampala, Uganda. By adopting the innovative Fukuoka Method, the project aims to rehabilitate 4.3 hectares of collapsed landfill within the 14.6-hectare Kiteezi dumpsite. It seeks to enhance environmental sustainability, mitigate public health risks, and safeguard the livelihoods of 20,000 residents in the surrounding area. The project aligns with Uganda’s urban development strategies and global frameworks, including the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Objectives 1. Rehabilitate the Kiteezi dumpsite and using the Fukuoka Method to prevent environmental and public health risks. 2. Strengthen KCCA’s technical capacity in sustainable solid waste management. 3. Reduce socio-economic vulnerabilities of waste pickers while promoting green business opportunities.
Expected Accomplishments 1. Enhanced environmental outcomes 2. Institutional strengthening 3. Community empowerment 4. Scalable solutions
Conclusion The Kiteezi Dumpsite Rehabilitation Project is a crucial step toward addressing Kampala’s waste management challenges while fostering sustainable urban development. By leveraging the innovative Fukuoka Method and building KCCA’s institutional capacity, the project will deliver long-term environmental, social, and economic benefits. This initiative sets a benchmark for sustainable waste management and contributes meaningfully to global environmental and urban resilience goals.
